issues.legal_issue: Criminal proceedings alleging acquisition of assets disproportionate to income cannot continue where the identical charge was rejected after a departmental inquiry and the prosecution’s central valuation evidence is materially unreliable and unexplained.
material_facts: The criminal case and the departmental case alleged the same acquisition of assets disproportionate to income.

After a detailed inquiry, the Central Vigilance Commission concluded that the officer’s savings exceeded the assets acquired and that the charge was not proved; the Union Public Service Commission concurred, and the officer was exonerated.
The prosecution relied centrally on a valuation of the officer’s building that differed substantially from an earlier valuation of the same property by the same engineers.
The prosecution valuation reports differed in their descriptions and rates, contained unexplained changes, and did not consistently support the valuation stated in the charge.
The engineers who prepared the disputed valuation were not produced at the departmental inquiry to explain the discrepancies or authenticate the report.
issues.conclusion: On the exceptional facts of the case, the criminal proceedings could not be pursued. The appeal was allowed and the impugned proceedings were quashed.
issues.legal_principle: An exoneration in departmental proceedings does not, by itself, bar a criminal prosecution, since the standard of proof in a criminal case is higher. However, under the principles governing the exercise of the inherent power under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and the extraordinary power under Article 226 of the Constitution, proceedings may be quashed in an appropriate exceptional case to prevent abuse of process or secure the ends of justice. The Court applied the categories illustrated in State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal, including cases where the uncontroverted allegations and supporting material do not disclose an offence, or where the allegations are inherently improbable. The Court treated the identical charge, the departmental exoneration, and the unexplained and doubtful valuation evidence together as making continuation of this prosecution unjustified; it did not establish a general rule that departmental exoneration automatically ends a criminal case.

rule.if: appeal_from_refusal_to_quash and criminal_disproportionate_assets_case and identical_departmental_charge and departmental_exoneration_after_inquiry and departmental_finding_assets_within_savings and prosecution_relies_on_disputed_valuation and valuation_reports_materially_inconsistent and valuation_authors_not_examined and changed_valuation_unexplained

predicates.appeal_from_refusal_to_quash: The accused appealed after a court refused to quash the criminal proceedings.
predicates.criminal_disproportionate_assets_case: The criminal proceeding alleged that the accused acquired assets disproportionate to income.
predicates.identical_departmental_charge: The departmental inquiry concerned the same charge as the criminal proceeding.
predicates.departmental_exoneration_after_inquiry: The accused was exonerated after a departmental inquiry into that charge.
predicates.departmental_finding_assets_within_savin: The departmental inquiry found that the accused’s savings exceeded the assets acquired.
predicates.prosecution_relies_on_disputed_valuation: The prosecution relied on a disputed valuation as a central basis for alleging disproportionate assets.
predicates.valuation_reports_materially_inconsisten: Valuations of the same property materially differed in their figures, descriptions, or methods.
predicates.valuation_authors_not_examined: The authors of the disputed valuation were not examined to explain or authenticate it.
predicates.changed_valuation_unexplained: The prosecution did not explain the material changes between the valuations.

issues.definition: When an appeal follows refusal to quash a criminal disproportionate-assets case, the identical charge has resulted in departmental exoneration based on savings exceeding assets, and the prosecution’s central valuation evidence is inconsistent, unauthenticated, and unexplained, the criminal proceedings cannot continue.
